cards.text: Paul is writing to God's people in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and he's just told them they've been made right with God through Jesus. Now he goes all the way back to Adam, the first man (Genesis 2:7). Sin came into the world through that one man, and death came in through sin.

cards.question: Sin came in through one man, and death came in through sin. According to Paul, who does death pass on to?

answers.text: Only the man who sinned first

cards.text: Paul says sin was in the world before the law was given, but sin isn't taken into account when there's no law. It's like speeding down a road before anybody puts up the sign: still too fast, but nothing to write on the ticket.

cards.question: Even with no law to count sin, death didn't take a day off. Paul says death reigned from Adam until which man?
From Adam to Moses, Israel's leader, death reigned even over people who didn't sin the way Adam did.

cards.text: Then Paul calls Adam a pattern of the One to come. Now you're speaking my language, friend: I'm a stamper, and patterns are my WHOLE job.

cards.question: Paul calls Adam a pattern of the One to come. Who is that One?
Paul puts Adam's trespass next to the gift that comes through Jesus. The gift is just like the trespass.
The many died by one man's trespass. In Paul's comparison, which one goes further?

cards.text: Paul's still comparing, and now he's counting, like me checking cookie boxes at closing time. The judgment brought condemnation, and the gift brought justification.

cards.question: The judgment that followed ___ sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed ___ trespasses brought justification.

cards.text: Then Paul says by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man. ONE man, and death's walking around like it owns the place.

cards.question: Paul says death keeps reigning over those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness.

cards.text: Now Paul ties the whole thing up like a cookie box. One trespass brought condemnation for all men.

cards.question: One trespass brought condemnation for all men. According to Paul, what brought justification and life for all men?
The many were made sinners through Adam's ___, and the many will be made righteous through Jesus' ___.

cards.text: Then Paul brings the law back into the picture, and friend, if you'd asked me why it came in, I'd have guessed wrong and LOUD.

cards.question: When the law came in, the trespass shrank.
When the law came in, sin increased. What did grace do where sin increased?
Paul lands it: just as ___ reigned in death, so also ___ might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

findings.problem: The opening card says Paul has 'just told them they've been made right with God through Jesus.' That fact comes from Romans 5:1-11, outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it. The card's other outside facts have references (Romans 1:1, 7 and Genesis 2:7).

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Romans 5:17's main point is that those who receive grace and the gift of righteousness 'reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ.' No card tells or asks this. The true or false card only makes the baker deny a statement Paul never makes. The text also doesn't say whether death keeps reigning over those who receive grace, so marking that statement False reads in something the text leaves open. A baker could argue the answer, and they would leave without the 'reign in life' contrast.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card tells almost nothing from Romans 5:20. Its line 'if you'd asked me why it came in, I'd have guessed wrong and LOUD' tells the baker that the expected answer is wrong. That gives away card 18, where the expected guess (the trespass shrank) is the false one.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Romans 5:20 gives a purpose: 'The law came in so that the trespass would increase.' Card 19's setup turns this into a sequence ('When the law came in, sin increased'), and card 18 frames it as a result too. No card tells the baker the 'so that' purpose, even though card 17 raises the question of why the law came in. This changes how the text connects the two things.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Two answers name something that goes further ('God's grace through Jesus Christ', 'Adam's one trespass'). The third, 'Neither one goes further', is a different kind of answer, so the answers aren't the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
